prompt:
A colleague has asked you to speak for a few minutes at a staff open day about the work you do, and has asked for a reply this week.

Write a letter to your colleague. In your letter:

- accept the invitation and say why you are glad to take part
- explain what you would like to talk about
- ask about the time you will have and the equipment in the room
instruction_line: You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. Write at least 150 words.
key_points: Acceptance must be stated clearly in the first paragraph — it should not be left vague
The reason for taking part should be backed with a short justification (sharing experience, introducing the team)
The content of the talk must be described concretely: which topic, how many points, why it is useful to the audience
The third bullet point expects two separate questions: the time available and the equipment in the room
Tone is semi-formal: address by name, polite but relaxed language suited to the workplace
common_mistakes: Writing a letter where it isn't clear whether the invitation is accepted or declined
Brushing off the talk's topic as just 'my job' without giving detail
Skipping either the question about time or the one about equipment
Slipping into overly formal phrases ('Yours faithfully') and losing the colleague-to-colleague tone
topic: replying to an invitation and asking about talk details
